'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Battle of Donbas (2022)|Battle of Donbas]]
****At least twelve civilians are killed and 25 others are injured by heavy [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] [[shell (projectile)|shelling]] in [[Donetsk Oblast]], according to a report by Governor [[Pavlo Kyrylenko]]. [https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-donetsk-government-and-politics-1fc51f17c706651bd2115cae3d2417f7 (AP)]  [https://www.voanews.com/a/ukrainian-officials-say-russian-shelling-kills-5-in-donetsk-/6647076.html (VOA)]
**[[Government and intergovernmental reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Latvia]] plans to reintroduce [[conscription]], which had been abolished in 2006, as a result of the [[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]. The final decision will be determined by the country's [[parliament]], the [[Saeima]]. [https://bnn-news.com/latvia-plans-to-adopt-a-general-state-defence-service-235940 (Baltic News Network)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/jul/06/latvia-to-reinstate-compulsory-military-service-as-russia-tensions-rise (AFP via ''The Guardian'')]
*[[Boko Haram insurgency]]
**[[Islamism|Islamist]] militants [[Prison breaks in Nigeria|attack a prison]] near [[Abuja]], [[Nigeria]], freeing 879 of the medium-security prison's 994 inmates. One prison guard is killed and three others are injured in the attack. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/jul/06/suspected-boko-haram-attack-frees-hundreds-of-prisoners-in-nigeria-abuja (''The Guardian'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*Chinese authorities give a tentative green light to [[Ant Group]] to revive its [[Initial public offering|initial public offering]] plans in both Shanghai and Hong Kong. [https://news.rthk.hk/rthk/en/component/k2/1652363-20220609.htm (RTHK)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2022 Marmolada serac collapse]]
**Two more people are found dead after the [[Marmolada]] [[serac]], in [[Italy]], collapsed three days ago, bringing the death toll to nine. Three other people are still missing. [https://www.repubblica.it/cronaca/2022/07/06/news/marmolada_crollo_ricerche_droni_quarto_giorno-356789420/ (''La Repubblica'')]
'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in China]]
***[[Xi'an]] is placed under [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] and mass testing is conducted in half of the city's districts after a cluster of cases in the city were traced back to six [[karaoke bar]]s. [https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/world-news/fresh-covid-outbreaks-put-millions-under-lockdown-in-china/articleshow/92691301.cms (''Economic Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Niue]]
***The [[New Zealand Defence Force]] says that, upon request by the government of [[Niue]], it is sending a team of civilian doctors, nurses, and defense personnel to help the territory deal with an outbreak of [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/nz-defence-force-medical-team-deployed-niue-after-covid-19-outbreak-2022-07-06/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Georgia Guidestones bombing]]
**The [[Georgia Guidestones]] in [[Elbert County, Georgia]], [[United States]], are partially destroyed in an explosion in what is a suspected bombing. A construction crew later pulls down the remaining parts of the structure for safety reasons. [https://www.nytimes.com/2022/07/06/us/georgia-guidestones-explosion.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2022/jul/06/georgia-monument-guidestones-americas-stonehenge-bombed (''The Guardian'')] [https://jp.reuters.com/article/us-georgia-explosion-idCAKBN2OI00M (Reuters)]
*[[2022 Sri Lankan political crisis]]
**Several opposition politicians are arrested in [[Colombo]], [[Sri Lanka]], after demanding the resignation of [[Prime Minister of Sri Lanka|Prime Minister]] [[Ranil Wickremesinghe]], who said yesterday that the country is "[[bankrupt]]". [https://economynext.com/sri-lanka-opposition-politicians-hirunika-premachandra-rehan-jayawickreme-arrested-at-protest-97023/ (Economy Next)]
*The [[government of Honduras]] releases a report stating that the deportation of [[Honduras|Honduran]] migrants from [[Mexico]] and the [[United States]] increased by 84.4% during the first half of the year. [https://www.infobae.com/america/agencias/2022/07/06/la-deportacion-de-migrantes-hondurenos-se-eleva-un-844-en-el-primer-semestre/ (Infobae)]
*A federal court in [[Buenos Aires]], [[Argentina]], sentences an ex-military officer to [[life in prison]] for homicides, kidnappings, tortures, and rape during the [[National Reorganization Process|military dictatorship]] that ruled the country between 1976 and 1983. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/argentina-jails-ex-military-officers-crimes-during-dictatorship-2022-07-06/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[July 2022 United Kingdom government crisis|2022 United Kingdom government crisis]]
**Multiple senior ministers of the [[United Kingdom]]'s [[Cabinet of the United Kingdom|Cabinet]], including newly appointed [[Chancellor of the Exchequer]] [[Nadhim Zahawi]], [[Home Secretary]] [[Priti Patel]], [[Secretary of State for Transport]] [[Grant Shapps]], and [[Secretary of State for Levelling Up, Housing and Communities]] [[Michael Gove]] tell [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]] to resign. Five additional ministers resign after dozens of others leave throughout the day, bringing the total of government departures to 38. [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2022/jul/06/michael-gove-boris-johnson-more-ministers-resign (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/boris-johnson-cabinet-resignation-b2117239.html (''The Independent'')] [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/uk-politics-62048657 (BBC News)]
**Boris Johnson fires Michael Gove after Gove called on Johnson to resign earlier in the day. A [[10 Downing Street]] official says that "you can’t have a snake who is not with you on any of the big arguments who then gleefully tells the press the leader has to go". [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/boris-johnson-sacks-michael-gove-b2117505.html (''The Independent'')]
**[[Simon Hart]] resigns as [[Secretary of State for Wales]] following Boris Johnson's refusal to leave office. [https://news.sky.com/story/simon-hart-resigns-as-secretary-of-state-for-wales-12647181 (Sky News)]
